messages:
joel_h: FYI I just observed a gap after the roles schema refactor backfill — around ~2.5k identities lost the default binding. Not all services, but a small percentage.
meera_k: ugh, when did the backfill run and which migration ID?
joel_h: migration `2026_03_roles_default_backfill` ran at 02:14 UTC. Seems like the update used an inner join that excluded rows with NULL role_id instead of assigning the default.
opsbot: deploy-bot: migration 2026_03_roles_default_backfill applied on prod-1 at 2026-03-18T02:14:03Z. 0 failed jobs.
alex_d: can we get a quick detection query so we know who is affected? also thumbs if we want an immediate rollback. :thumbsup:
meera_k: yes please paste the detection SQL. we'll need counts by service/team and a list of highest-privilege principals.
joel_h: detection query I ran:```sql
-- find principals with no effective role after backfill
SELECT p.id, p.type, p.owner_team, coalesce(r.role_name, '<<MISSING>>') as role_name
FROM principals p
LEFT JOIN principal_roles r ON p.id = r.principal_id
WHERE p.created_at < '2026-03-18' AND (r.role_name IS NULL OR r.role_name = '')
LIMIT 100;```
I got ~2,432 rows and 47 of them are service_accounts with previously expected 'reader' default.
riley_s: KMS audit shows a handful of service tokens used for replay tests failing 403 around 02:20 UTC, matches timeline. can attach logs.
meera_k: ok split work: joel can you run counts by team and a rollback plan. alex and riley can validate KMS/audit anomalies and confirm whether any retries caused auth failures. I'll coordinate comms.
joel_h: rollback plan options: 1) re-run corrected backfill with `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` / coalesce to set default where NULL — quick and idempotent. 2) partial rollback by restoring DB snapshot from 02:05 UTC and re-applying later migrations — more invasive. I prefer option 1 for lower blast radius.
alex_d: agree option 1. can you share the exact SQL you'll run and the safety checks?
joel_h: SQL to run (dry-run first):```sql
-- dry run: show rows we'd touch
SELECT count(*) FROM principals p
LEFT JOIN principal_roles r ON p.id = r.principal_id
WHERE p.created_at < '2026-03-18' AND (r.role_name IS NULL OR r.role_name = '');

-- upsert to set default 'reader'
INSERT INTO principal_roles (principal_id, role_name, added_by, added_at)
SELECT p.id, 'reader', 'migration-corrected', now()
FROM principals p
LEFT JOIN principal_roles r ON p.id = r.principal_id
WHERE p.created_at < '2026-03-18' AND (r.role_name IS NULL OR r.role_name = '');
-- note: principal_roles has unique(principal_id), DB will error on conflict if constraint exists so use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING in prod run if needed
```
I'll run dry-run counts first and post results.
meera_k: ensure we also check for principals that previously had a non-default (higher) role that might have been accidentally cleared — we must not overwrite existing explicit roles.
joel_h: confirmed — my query only targets NULL/empty roles. won't touch any non-null roles.
opsbot: alert: Service token auth failure spike (403) between 02:19-02:25 UTC — 32 events, severity low.
riley_s: attaching sample KMS error: `access denied: principal p-44321 missing role` — looks consistent with missing role. I've parked the full log in /infra/alerts/2188881111.log.
alex_d: can we throttle the backfill to a canary: run on 10 principals from different teams and monitor?\meera_k: yes do a canary. joel, pick 10 (mix of service and user), run the insert with a tag `migration-corrected-canary` and monitor. If green, we proceed in 30m batches.
joel_h: doing canary now (will post counts). dry-run count = 2432. canary subset = 10 principals chosen across 5 teams. will push canary up with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and `RETURNING principal_id` so we can verify changed rows.
joel_h: canary applied: returned 9 rows (one already had role). waiting 10m to see retries.
meera_k: checking auth logs — 10m window looks clean, no 403 spikes for those principals.
riley_s: KMS errors for other principals still present, working through batch mapping.
alex_d: after canary success, run 30m batches. coordinate with oncall to watch SLOs. also add a migration audit log entry with the migration-corrections KMS KID we used.
joel_h: will run batches: plan 8 batches of ~300, pause 10m between. posting start times as I go.
meera_k: I'll open a short incident note for compliance with audit trail and notify CS for customers that had token issues. tag: @security-oncall if escalation needed.
opsbot: note: scheduled job `auth-slo-watcher` will alert at 1.5% 403 increase.
meera_k: thanks — quick heads up to the team: after the refactor let's include a `SELECT` check verifying no NULL role_name rows before marking migration done in future. small follow-up action item.
joel_h: logged follow-up in #eng-security-runbook: add preflight check for `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM principal_roles WHERE role_name IS NULL)` before marking migration.
alex_d: good. once full backfill completes, let's add an integration test that simulates principals with NULL role and ensures default gets assigned.
meera_k: agreed. closing loop: current state = canary success, running batch 1 now at 2026-03-18T03:05:12Z. will update.
